preamble: The solution to 8 across 17 down (not further defined) suggests how those to 10 other clues must be treated before entry in the grid. Ten more (otherwise normal) clues contain one or two superfluous words; each of these defines one of the thematic 8 acrosses. All letter counts are for the solutions to be entered in the grid.

clue.text: Vases — not Eric's — picked up

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, so the answer is a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Eric Morecambe called his partner Ernie Wise Ern, so what belongs to Eric's partner is Ern's

explanation.surface: A collector insists the vases on show are not Eric's, then lifts them.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a British comedy double act, Eric and Ernie, so 'not Eric's' points to Ern's. The partner theme is at work here too, in the wordplay rather than the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a tall rounded vessel, often ornamental, the same family of container as a vase.

clue.text: Loos maybe are something special in North America

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for an are, a metric unit of area

indicators.note: one piece set in the other, so the special something sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: it, as in the It girl, is that special quality that sets someone apart

explanation.surface: Wondering whether lavatories count as a treat in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Loos is not toilets but Anita Loos, author of Gentlemen Prefer Blondes. The clue gives ANITA; IT swaps for GIN, its partner in GIN AND IT, so the grid takes ANGINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is the first name of the writer Anita Loos, so a Loos may be an Anita.

clue.text: Substantial resistance inside prison

indicators.note: the letter for resistance goes inside the word for substantial

parts.note: substantial means large, big

explanation.surface: Heavy opposition from within a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the symbol for electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a prison, originally the cell block aboard a naval ship.

clue.text: A bit much everybody arriving for tea!

indicators.note: a bit of a phrase is a stretch of its letters, here the run across the join of much and arriving

parts.note: taken as written; its last two letters are kept
taken as written; its first two letters are kept

explanation.surface: It is rather a lot when the whole family turns up for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everybody' is a spare word: it defines ONE AND ALL, the pair swapped in 18 Down. Without it, the letters run straight from much into arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is British slang for tea, from the Chinese word cha.

clue.text: A lot of bad dreams about fish

indicators.note: about can mean around in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
a lot of a thing is most but not all of it, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler troubled by recurring nightmares about fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'about' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Smear dab is an old regional name for the lemon sole, a flatfish of northern European waters.

clue.text: Good drink? Free bars here

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A pub boasting good beer and free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' is a spare word: it defines GIN AND IT, gin with Italian vermouth, the pair swapped in 2 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a framework of crossing bars, so bars are found there.

clue.text: Suspend pandemic measure — can one get upset about call?

indicators.note: the overturned letters go about, around, the word for call
something upset is turned over, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
I is the Roman numeral for one
to call something a name is to term it

explanation.surface: A question of whether lockdown can be lifted without a row over the decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pandemic measure' is a spare phrase: it defines TEST AND TRACE, the UK's Covid scheme, the pair swapped in 14 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or interrupt something for a time.

clue.text: Bit worrying Pep's warning

indicators.note: worrying at something is pulling it about, so these letters are tugged into a new order

parts.note: a bit is a part of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans fret over a warning from Pep Guardiola, the Manchester City manager.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says this answer is not further defined: the whole clue is wordplay. It names the theme, in which ten answers swap one half of a familiar pair for the other before entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Partner swapping is exchanging one member of a couple for another, which is what the ten treated answers do with paired words.

clue.text: Agreed to come in for a game

indicators.note: to come in tells us the word for agreed must enter the word for for, sitting inside it

parts.note: per means for, as in so much per head
OK means agreed, as in an okayed plan

explanation.surface: Someone finally consents to join in a round of some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' here is not a link but the Latin-derived PER (as in 'per person'), and 'to come in' puts OK inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game of betting and bluffing, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Going over lines mostly pissed in rehearsal

indicators.note: one piece goes over the other, covering it, so the drunk letters wrap around the lines
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pissed is British slang for drunk
RY is the crossword abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: An actor half-cut while running through the script before opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives DRY RUN. Under the theme DRY swaps for its partner in HOME AND DRY, so the grid takes HOME RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a practice performance or trial before the real thing, which is what a rehearsal is.

clue.text: US politician, very close, lightly touching Queen

parts.note: kissing can mean touching gently, as a ball kisses another in snooker

explanation.surface: A Washington figure caught brushing up against the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very close' is one of the spare words: it defines TOUCH AND GO, the pair swapped in 27 Across. Set aside, the clue is a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kissinger was a US Secretary of State and National Security Adviser under Nixon and Ford.

clue.text: Go off beer, drinking Double Diamonds

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing inside it, so the beer holds the diamonds

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
D is diamonds in card notation, so two of them are DD

explanation.surface: Swearing off beer while knocking back Double Diamond, a British bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Double Diamond is a British beer brand, which makes the surface read as one drink inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle go bad, so to addle is to go off in the sense of spoiling.

clue.text: Ruling in the club — no secure parking

indicators.note: no says a letter is taken away, as on a sign forbidding it
parking names the letter that goes, P being the road-sign symbol for a car park

parts.note: in the club is British slang for pregnant

explanation.surface: A members' club rule: no secure parking on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secure' is a spare word: it defines HOME AND DRY, the pair swapped in 9 Across. In the club, from 'in the pudding club', is British slang for expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant who rules in her own right.

clue.text: Take flight, land at Heathrow, not Gatwick (aircrew initially unhappy)

indicators.note: unhappy letters are disturbed, so they are rearranged
initially takes the first letter of each word

parts.note: taken as written; the five words supply their first letters

explanation.surface: A flight diverted to Heathrow rather than Gatwick, leaving the cabin crew grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take flight' is a spare phrase: it defines CUT AND RUN, the pair swapped in 26 Down. The initials come from at, Heathrow, not, Gatwick and aircrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country in West Africa, a land in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: Go to embrace one girl

indicators.note: embracing someone holds them inside your arms, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt
an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone urged to go and hug a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives TRACEY. TRACE swaps for TEST, its partner in TEST AND TRACE, the UK's Covid tracking scheme, so the grid takes TESTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey is a girl's given name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Cleaner's easily distracted at first entering private area of house

indicators.note: the two letters enter, going inside the word for cleaner

parts.note: a broom is a cleaner for sweeping floors

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each word

parts.note: taken as written; the two words supply their first letters

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained cleaner wanders into the family's private quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom is the most private room in a home, where one sleeps.

clue.text: Extra posh bloke going round country

indicators.note: going round turns the word back on itself, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: a nob is British slang for a toff, an upper-class man
the US, short for the United States, is a country

explanation.surface: A toff touring the country with something extra in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is something extra, paid or given over and above what is due.

clue.text: Gradual damage affected one rose tree

indicators.note: affected means changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rose bush suffering slow decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gradual damage' is a spare phrase: it defines WEAR AND TEAR, the pair swapped in 22 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow tree whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Sees son has knocked back Scotch

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to put a stop to it

explanation.surface: A father notices his son has downed a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SPOTS. POTS swaps for PANS, its partner in POTS AND PANS, so the grid takes SPANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it, so spots matches sees.

clue.text: See 8 across
Market tax could be legal, as town's leader admitted

indicators.note: something admitted is let in, so the letter goes inside the rearranged words
could be says these letters might become something else, a hint to rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the word's opening letter is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mayor concedes that a levy on traders might be lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives STALLAGE. ALL swaps for ONE, its partner in ONE AND ALL, so the grid takes STONE AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stallage is the rent or toll paid for setting up a stall in a market, an old form of trading tax.

clue.text: Shopper at first in wrong store

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: taken as written; only its first letter is used
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper who walked into the wrong shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' is a spare word: it defines B AND Q, a British DIY store chain, the pair swapped in 20 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wrong, a moral offence.

clue.text: Left both inside and out — it's a comfort in retirement

indicators.note: one piece placed inside the other, so the letter sits within the word for left

parts.note: quit is a past tense meaning left, departed
both says left is used twice: once as the word outside and once as its abbreviation inside

explanation.surface: Someone who has walked out is consoled by thoughts of their pension.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives QUILT. Q swaps for B, its partner in B AND Q, a British DIY store chain, so the grid takes BUILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement here is going to bed, and a quilt is a warm bed covering, in America called a comforter.

clue.text: Randy hosts will presumably not vote for Starmer

wordplay.words: will presumably not vote for Starmer
wordplay.note: read as a speaker's self-description: three short words saying they belong to the Conservative party, so are unlikely to back Keir Starmer, the Labour leader

explanation.surface: Lustful party hosts who are unlikely to support Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' is a spare word: it defines ANT AND DEC, the British TV presenters, the pair swapped in 31 Across. The phrase splits as AM A TORY, the Tories being the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory means relating to sexual love, and so carries the same sense as randy, eager for sex.

clue.text: Invest? I answer doubtfully

indicators.note: an answer given doubtfully is shaky and uncertain, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether to put money in, someone replies without conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SWEAR IN. WEAR swaps for TEAR, its partner in WEAR AND TEAR, so the grid takes STEARIN, a fat used in candles.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone with an office is to install them formally, which is what swearing them in does.

clue.text: Itches to break moral code

indicators.note: broken up, the word's letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Urges that tempt someone to break their principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right and wrong that govern conduct.

clue.text: November 1 — special day once

definitions.note: the answer is a plural form but names a single day of the old calendar

parts.note: N is November in the radio alphabet
the numeral 1 written out as a word

explanation.surface: A note in the diary: the first of November, a special day long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the nones was the ninth day before the ides, a fixed day in each month.

clue.text: Dog biting Queen's backside finally — clear out!

indicators.note: biting puts something between the jaws, inside the dog

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
R stands for Regina, the queen

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter

parts.note: taken as written; only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A dog nipping the Queen's bottom, and the order to get out.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to clear out or rid of unwanted things or people.

clue.text: Caught taking pickup — that's smart

indicators.note: the catch takes the truck on, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a ute is an Australian name for a pickup truck

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught off a slow lob, and the crowd calls it clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives CUTE. CUT swaps for RUN, its partner in CUT AND RUN, so the grid takes RUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in American usage means clever or shrewd, often a little too clever.

clue.text: Warehouse sink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a godown is a warehouse in India and East Asia
second meaning: to go down is to sink

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions give GODOWN. GO swaps for TOUCH, its partner in TOUCH AND GO, so the grid takes TOUCHDOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Godown, from Malay, is a dockside storehouse; read as two words, go down means sink beneath the surface.

clue.text: Play receiving national award

indicators.note: the play word receives, takes in, the abbreviation

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: A stage show picking up a prize from the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tony is a Broadway theatre award, so it fits play and award in one.

clue.text: Drive up, turn twice around — language!

indicators.note: the two turns go around the reversed road word

parts.note: a U-turn is a turn, so two of them give two Us

indicators.note: in a down clue up reads a word from the bottom, so it is reversed

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive

explanation.surface: A motorist driving uphill, doing two U-turns and swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language of South Asia, the national language of Pakistan.

clue.text: Maneater's not finished Roger off

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
not finished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A predator interrupted mid-meal, and Roger gets away.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre in folklore is a giant who eats people, a maneater.

clue.text: Lack of bread containers around — go figure

indicators.note: the bread phrase goes around the short word

parts.note: no naan, the Indian flatbread, gives NO NAN
taken as written

explanation.surface: An empty bread bin, and the shrug of go figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containers' is a spare word: it defines POTS AND PANS, the pair swapped in 17 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a plane figure with nine sides.

clue.text: Star earns a bomb — about time!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the letter for time
to bomb is to blow up, so the letters of these words are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor finally lands a huge pay cheque, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives ANTARES. ANT swaps for DEC, his partner in ANT AND DEC, a British TV presenting duo, so the grid takes DECARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright red supergiant at the heart of the constellation Scorpius.
